business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Multi-Axis Computerized Numerical Control Metal Centers

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: China-France Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 26 November 2007, entered into force 9 January 2010)
France-China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (signed 30 May 1984, as amended by Protocol of 26 November 2013, entered into force 1 January 2015)
EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (CAI, signed 30 December 2020; pending ratification)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title VII — Articles L.227-1 to L.227-30 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); general company provisions, Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10; dematerialised corporate formalities governed by Decree No. 2021-300 of 18 March 2021 implementing the national business formalities portal (guichet unique).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) maintaining the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), with territorial jurisdiction in the departement of the registered office; filings are lodged electronically through the single national portal operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) together with the unified incorporation declaration (M0) and all required supporting annexes, submitted via the INPI one-stop shop.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for an SAS (Article L.227-2); capital may be fixed at EUR 1 and any amount is freely determined in the Articles. Cash contributions must be deposited and blocked in a French credit institution, with a notary or with the Caisse des Depots et Consignations, and released only upon issuance of the RCS registration certificate (Kbis); in-kind contributions exceeding EUR 7,500 require a statutory appraiser (commissaire aux apports). No formal escrow account is otherwise mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [Company Name] SAS.

RESOLUTION 1 — Share Subscription: The shareholders acknowledge that the share capital of EUR [Amount] has been fully subscribed and released as set out in the Articles, and all cash contributions are deposited and blocked under Article L.227-2 of the French Commercial Code.

RESOLUTION 2 — Registered Office: The registered office is fixed at [Address], within the Court Registry of [City]; the President is authorized to execute any lease and complete all RCS filings.

RESOLUTION 3 — Officers: The shareholders appoint [Full Name] as President (Legal Representative) with the broadest powers to bind the Company, and authorize the publication of the legal notice and submission to the INPI incorporation portal.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), acting through the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE), administered via the impots.gouv.fr portal; customs and export controls are administered by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) through the SOPRANO customs clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated SAS held by non-resident shareholders: (1) file the articles of association (statuts) and incorporation particulars via the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; (2) obtain the 9-digit SIREN and 14-digit SIRET identification numbers automatically allocated by INSEE; (3) complete the tax registration file with the competent SIE, which attributes the statutory tax identification number and, where registration is mandatory, the intra-Community VAT number in the format 'FR + 11 digits'; (4) register with the commercial and companies register (RCS), the URSSAF social security body, and the DGDDI for statistical and customs purposes; (5) if the SAS is not established in any EU Member State, appoint a VAT fiscal representative in France under Article 289 A of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI) for VAT compliance and payments.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: an SAS is a commercial company with legal personality and is subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés - IS) under Article 206-1 CGI on its worldwide taxable profits, with a standard headline corporate income tax rate of 25%; foreign shareholders are not taxable in France on retained profits, but distributions to non-residents are subject to dividend withholding tax at 25% (source taxation), reduced or exempted under applicable tax treaties and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not adopt a US-style check-the-box election; entity classification is fixed by law. The principal statutory elections available to an SAS include: (1) the option under Article 239 bis AB CGI to be taxed under the personal income tax regime for the first five fiscal years where revenue thresholds are met; (2) the election to apply the fiscal integration regime (intégration fiscale) under Articles 223 A et seq. CGI, allowing the SAS to consolidate directly or indirectly held 95% subsidiaries for corporate income tax purposes; (3) the parent-subsidiary participation exemption election under Articles 145 and 216 CGI for qualifying shareholdings; (4) hybrid and reverse-hybrid mismatch election mechanisms under Article 212 bis CGI transposing ATAD 2, including elective alignment of tax characterisation between French and foreign jurisdictions; and (5) VAT-specific elections such as the option to tax immovable property under Article 260 CGI or the option for rates applicable to certain taxable supplies. No generic entity-level check-the-box mechanism exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic franchise en base de TVA small-business exemption: EUR 85,000 annual taxable turnover for principal supplies of goods such as CNC machine tools, and EUR 37,500 for supplies of services (Articles 293 B to 293 B ter CGI). Non-established foreign suppliers may not invoke this franchise and must VAT-register from the first taxable transaction in France. Intra-Community distance sales to non-taxable consumers are aggregated through the Union One-Stop-Shop with the EUR 10,000 pan-EU distance-sales threshold, while imports and domestic local sales are not covered by that threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured B2B e-invoicing and transactional e-reporting, introduced by the Loi de finances 2022 and the e-invoicing decree 2024-1127: from 1 September 2026 all taxable persons must be able to receive structured electronic invoices and large and medium enterprises must issue them; from 1 September 2027 the emission obligation extends to all SMEs and micro-enterprises. Invoices must be exchanged through a registered Partner Dematerialisation Platform (PDP) or the public Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) using EN 16931-compliant formats (Factur-X, UBL, CII); e-reporting of transaction data to DGFiP operates in near-real time and serves as the fiscal clearance mechanism, replacing any physical stamping or digital fiscal stamp for ordinary B2B supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A French SAS manufacturing multi-axis CNC milling centres may apply the 0% TVA rate to: (1) definitive exports of machinery to destinations outside the European Union under Article 262-I-1° CGI, provided the goods physically leave the EU territory under a duly accepted export customs declaration; (2) intra-Community dispatches to EU VAT-registered customers, where the customer's valid VAT number is stated and the supply qualifies under Article 262 ter-I CGI; and (3) ancillary international transport, handling, and intermediary services directly connected to such exports under Article 262-II CGI. The 0% rate is denied where the exporter merely delivers goods on a domestic basis, where the transport documentation does not prove physical exit, or where the services are performed for the exporter's own account; the exporter must hold complete contemporaneous proof before the tax authority.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Document Administratif Unique / DAU) formally accepted by DGDDI
Bill of Lading (Connaissement) or equivalent transport document proving physical exit from EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (attestation de rapatriement des recettes d'exportation) and wire-transfer evidence confirming receipt of export proceeds within the applicable repatriation deadline
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to joint audit by DGFiP and DGDDI, with the documentary bundle scrutinised to verify physical export, counterparty identity, and the genuine repatriation of proceeds within the 180-day deadline after customs clearance. Where zero-rating is unjustified or documents are false, DGFiP recharges output VAT at 20%, disallows corresponding input VAT recovery (Articles 266, 271, and 272 CGI), and applies the statutory penalties: 40% of the net tax for bad faith and 80% for abusive conduct or fraudulent manoeuvres under Article 1729 CGI, plus monthly late-payment interest under Article 1727 CGI. Customs sanctions under Article 413-1 of the Code des douanes may reach one to two times the value of the goods, with seizure and confiscation of the exported machinery; criminal tax fraud under Article 1741 CGI is punishable by up to five years' imprisonment and a fine of EUR 500,000. Retrospective clawback extends over the general six-year limitation period of the French tax code, or ten years where the taxpayer has concealed the relevant facts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) and the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR), with cross-border capital movement oversight coordinated with the Minister of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates a fully convertible current account under EU Capital Movement Directive (88/361/EEC) and OECD Article VIII obligations; the euro is freely transferable. Capital account transactions are also liberalised within the EU and toward third countries, subject to EU sanctions, counter-cyclical measures, and statistical declarations to the Banque de France under Regulation (EU) No 184/2016 and French Monetary and Financial Code (CMF). Profit remittances by a French SAS are permitted without prior authorisation, but must be processed through compliant banking channels with appropriate economic substance documentation, transfer pricing documentation, and withholding tax formality verification (e.g., EU Interest-Royalty Directive where applicable, tax residency certificates, and beneficial ownership declarations) to avoid recharacterisation as constructive dividends or hidden distributions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory export proceeds surrender or conversion obligation. Export receipts in foreign currency may be retained on foreign currency accounts, transferred abroad, or converted freely. However, exporters must declare cross-border payments to the Banque de France when monthly cumulative flows exceed EUR 750,000 or the individual transaction exceeds EUR 150,000 for statistical balance-of-payments purposes, under CMF Article R.152-3 and Banque de France instruction No 2014-01. For CNY-denominated receipts arising from the sale of CNC five-axis milling centers to Chinese counterparties, settlement may be made directly in CNY via authorised correspondent banks, but accounting records must reflect the EUR-equivalent under French GAAP for statutory financial statements, and treasury must monitor ECB reference rates for accuracy.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE / Banque Populaire & Caisse d'Épargne group

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-LOW for use as the primary treasury rail. Offshore Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) operating under EU e-money directives (EMD2) may open settlement accounts in France only if licensed in an EU/EEA member state and passporting through ACPR, or if licensed by the ACPR directly. Non-EEA EMIs (e.g., UK-licensed EMIs post-Brexit, Singapore-based digital banks) cannot accept French client deposits or operate as principal settlement banks without a full credit institution license, and they generally lack access to the Banque de France's Target2 settlement system, meaning liquidity positions would require correspondent banking through an authorised French bank. EMIs may be used narrowly for ancillary payment collection in small-value domestic receivables, but are unsuitable for high-value CNC machinery export LCs and SWIFT MT103 clearing, and their inability to provide trade finance instruments such as standby LCs or discounting facilities creates unacceptable settlement risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident-owned SAS, French banks generally require at least one physical onboarding meeting with the legal representatives or beneficial owners holding >25% of shares or voting rights. Remote onboarding is possible using ACPR-compliant video identification (AUDESP / CNIL-accepted processes), but most Tier-1 banks impose physical presence for the CEO or the authorised signatory, particularly because the ISIC 2822 CNC machinery sector is categorised as High-Risk for dual-use and classified-export controls. The physical meeting should occur in an EU branch or French head office; remote video interviews are accepted only after a pre-existing banking relationship or for a sub-account opened under a group facility. The chairman of the SAS or the corporate officer holding the power to sign the banking mandate must attend the initial KYC interview; the bank may accept a notarised power-of-attorney from a foreign shareholder, but discretion remains with the compliance committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder with ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) in the PRC and unexplained capital injection source
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate register extract (Kbis) under 24 hours old; SAS articles of association and share transfer deeds; notarised and apostilled legalisation of the shareholder's constitutive documents; UBO declaration; bank reference letters from the injecting institution; audited financial statements or liquidity proof; source-of-wealth statement certified by a law firm; proof of economic substance in France (office lease, French payroll, operational capex invoices for the CNC assembly facility); tax residency certificates of the shareholder and certification that no shell company structure is present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export classification and dual-use concern for CNC five-axis milling centers under EU Dual-Use Regulation (EU) 2021/821 (per export control list 2B001 for precision machine tools)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: End-User Certificate (EUC) from the Chinese purchaser; final destination declaration; end-use statement certified by the buyer's regulator (where applicable); ICC Terms of Trade and commercial contract with full product technical specifications; export authorisation or general export licence EU001 applied for; compliance manual covering restricted-country screening; denial-list screening (EU, UN, OFAC) of all transaction parties; internal compliance program (ICP) certification; historical track record of similar authorised shipments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk correspondent clearing for outbound payments to entities in a sanctioned or watch-listed jurisdiction adjacent to the PRC (e.g., Hong Kong SAR, Singapore, UAE re-export hubs)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compliance-prepared transaction explanation memorandum; full chain of title invoices and packing lists; bill of lading and forwarder receipt; attested order documents from the final end-user; down-stream product classification and project description; screening reports from LexisNexis / World-Check showing no sanctions match; SWIFT-wide party identifier (Bank Identifier Code) of the receiving bank; confirmation that the beneficiary is not on the EU consolidated financial sanctions list; contract clause specifying no transshipment via prohibited entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Milling center price exceeds the bank's internal threshold requiring enhanced due diligence (EDD) on related-party debt or shareholder loans financing the French entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transfer pricing documentation (TP Documentation File and Master File under French Article L.13-AA, L.13-AB of the Tax Procedure Code); intercompany loan agreements with arm's-length interest rates supported by OECD comparability analysis; board resolutions approving the treasury capitalization; group cash flow forecasts; external accountant attestation; copy of the cross-border capital declaration submitted to Banque de France; evidence of non-tax-haven jurisdiction and absence of hybrid mismatch under ATAD.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a French SAS established with minimal statutory capital (no minimum, but commonly EUR 1 or 100), inbound shareholder capital injections from non-residents must be routed through a French authorised bank or via a correspondent bank with a SEPA or SWIFT-compliant wire (SWIFT MT103). The flow must be denominated in EUR for the capital subscription account and reflected in the 'Capital souscrit non libéré' or 'Capital appelé, versé' accounting lines. For injections above EUR 150,000, a declaration to the Banque de France must be submitted electronically via the 'Déclaration de Transaction' portal within 20 business days after the month-end of the transaction. Supporting documents: shareholder resolution, bank's anti-money-laundering KYC check, proof of source of funds, and the notarised deed of incorporation. No exchange control approval is required, but banks may require a 'Code Motif' (purpose code) for the wire, typically 'S1301 – Apport en capital' (non-resident direct investment) or 'T401 – Crédit commercial' if structured as shareholder loan; using a wrong purpose code can trigger immediate compliance review and potential blocking.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail is SWIFT MT103 for straight commercial payments covering spare parts procurement, agent commissions, and freight or insurance costs. For high-value CNC machine-tool settlement with end customers, the mandatory rail is an Irrevocable Documentary Letter of Credit (Commercial LC) issued by the buyer's bank, confirmed by a French or EU bank, payable at sight or deferred, subject to UCP 600 and eUCP where applicable. The French Bank (confirming or advising bank) will route via MT700/MT710 messages and settle against presentation of: commercial invoice, full set of clean-on-board ocean/multimodal bills of lading, packing list, certificate of origin (EUR.1/EUR-MED or Form A where applicable), insurance policy, inspection certificate, and the End-User Certificate for export-controlled milling centers. Alternative clearing rails for EU intra-community payments are SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT) for amounts under USD 100k equivalent; for cross-border non-EU transfers exceeding this threshold, SWIFT MT103 is mandatory. Standby Letters of Credit (SBLC) or performance guarantees may be issued via SWIFT MT760 to support installation and commissioning milestones. Hedging-related outflows are settled via MT202 cover payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/CNY outright forward contracts (plain vanilla, deliverable, bilateral ISDA/IECA based)
EUR/USD deliverable forwards to hedge dollar-denominated component imports
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNY where permitted by the French bank's internal risk policy and where the underlying trade is economically hedged
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/CNY) with term sheets under ISDA 2002, subject to bilateral credit support annex (CSA)
FX options (call/put, zero-cost collars) used exclusively to hedge confirmed purchase orders, not speculative treasury positions
Commodity-linked and trade-finance hedges embedded in the export LC contract, where legally separable and documented separately

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax (IS) for qualifying net taxable income; reduced bracket of 15% applies to the first €42,000 of annual profit for qualifying SMEs meeting the statutory tests
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: CIR research tax credit (30% of eligible R&D spend up to €100 million; 5% above); CII innovation tax credit (20% up to €400,000 of qualifying innovation expenditure); Patent/IP box effective rate of 10% on net qualifying patent licensing/assignment income subject to the R&D nexus ratio; 95% participation-exemption on qualifying dividends under the régime mère-fille; unlimited tax-loss carryforward subject to the annual cap of €1 million plus 50% of taxable income over €1 million (no statutory year limit)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (CERFA n°15997) — Déclaration de résultats; annexed schedules 2050 through 2059 for balance sheet, P&L, fixed assets, depreciation, provisions, debt, and R&D; mandatory e-filing via the impots.gouv.fr 'EFI/EDI' professional portal (TéléIR / liasse fiscale). The related-party disclosure Form 2257-SD is appended when the group turnover threshold is met.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual liasse fiscale filed once per fiscal year; advance instalments of IS are paid quarterly on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December via the e-payment system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal years closing on 31 December, the return must be transmitted electronically no later than the second business day following 1 May of the following year; for closing dates other than 31 December, no later than the second business day following expiry of the three-month period after the fiscal year close (extended electronically by a few days for EDI filers).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN, SIRET, APE/NAF code, registered office address, fiscal year opening and closing dates, date of incorporation, legal form (SAS), share capital paid up, and the shareholder identity where a single member or parent holds control.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French SAS is a French tax-resident entity regardless of foreign ownership; enter the French registered office and, if the SAS is a 100% foreign-owned conduit without French premises, insert the ultimate foreign parent's identity and its jurisdiction of residence in the shareholders section; the non-resident parent cannot be substituted as the reporting entity for the French return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C — Box 330 (Bénéfice comptable) / Box 331 (Déficit comptable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net income or net loss before tax derived from French GAAP (plan comptable général), after depreciation, provisions, and inventory valuation adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record French statutory accounts of the SAS; transactions with the foreign parent must be booked at arm's length fair value, and any non-arm's length intercompany recharges must be reversed or recharacterized in the reconciliation grid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal add-backs (non-deductible expenses, taxes on non-deductible provisions, excess depreciation on non-eco vehicles, interest add-backs, unreported penalties) and tax credits/loss offsets applied in the tax reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back disallowed cross-border charges (e.g., royalties paid to a non-resident if substance and arm's length benefit are unproven, thin-capitalization excess interest under the 25% earnings-stripping rule of CGI Article 212 bis); deductible CIR credits are recorded even when the entity is loss-making and recoverable against future IS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3527 — Résultat fiscal avant imputation des déficits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result before utilization of previous years' carried-forward tax losses (déficits reportables).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate the result using only French-source taxable items attributed to the SAS; offshore intercompany arrangements shifting profit to the foreign parent must be neutralized under Article 57 CGI before this line is finalized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3508 (line of imputations) — Déficits antérieurs imputés
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of prior-year French tax losses applied against the current-year taxable income; the annual off set is limited to €1 million plus 50% of the taxable base exceeding €1 million; no fixed year-expiry applies to carried-forward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Keep the déficit follow-up ledger (suivi des déficits) available for audit; a change of control of the SAS can trigger forfeiture of loss carryforwards unless the business activity and the original shareholding condition continuity tests are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 365 — Base imposable au taux normal (IS at 25%) and Box 363 — Base au taux réduit (15% SME bracket)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Splitting the final taxable profit into the reduced-rate base (first €42,000 for SMEs meeting the statutory definition) and the standard-rate base taxable at 25%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the SME criteria (headcount below 250? Actually French definition: fewer than 250 employees and either turnover ≤ €50 million or balance sheet ≤ €43 million, paid-up capital 75% held by individuals/SMEs) — a foreign corporate parent holding more than 25% of the capital disqualifies the reduced-rate bracket; recalculate the base at 25% accordingly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 360/361/362 — IS brut, contribution sociale sur l'IS, and tax credits (CIR/CII)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of statutory IS before and after credits; the 3.3% social surcharge applies to IS exceeding €763,000 for companies with turnover above €7.63 million.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No separate non-resident procedure: the French SAS itself is assessed; foreign-source taxes and foreign tax credits (crédit d'impôt étranger) are entered by the French entity on the basis of the applicable DTA, not by the foreign shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2257-SD — Déclaration des opérations avec des entreprises liées
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual disclosure of controlled transactions (purchases, sales, royalties, interest, management fees) and margins realized; required where the French entity or its worldwide group exceeds the statutory turnover threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Map every transaction stream with the non-resident parent and sister companies; append functional-risk matrix, benchmark range, and split of intangibles for the five-axis CNC milling scope; an incomplete 2257-SD gives the administration a legal basis to apply the 80% sanctions regime and to shift taxation to the foreign parent's margin level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late payment are governed by CGI Articles 1728 and 1731: automatic late-payment interest of 0.2% per month (intérêt de retard); a 10% late-filing surcharge when the return is filed within 30 days of the formal notice; 40% when the return is filed after the 30-day notice; 80% where an 'activité occulte' (undisclosed activity) or fraudulent maneuvers are established; plus a fixed €150 fine per missing or non-electronically transmitted schedule and a €15 fine per paper statement. The repeated or fraudulent failure carries criminal exposure under Article 1741 (see fatal red flags).
